title: time-sliced-fairshare-batcher-with-grace-handling
author: Samira Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring p99 latency spikes and transient starvation for low-rate tenants when heavy KV-pinned requests or long-context streams arrived concurrently. Previous fixes (cohorting, ticket leases) reduced incidents but emphasized trade-offs between fairness and utilization. This PR introduces a time-sliced fair-share windowing scheduler with a short "grace token" mechanism to avoid premature preemption of in-flight small requests and to reduce KV-pin starvation while preserving high throughput.

Design summary: Implement a scheduler that divides time into micro-windows (configurable default 10ms) and enforces proportional CPU/slot shares per tenant/route within each window. To avoid pathological preemption of short requests, we introduce a per-request grace token budget (leaky-bucket per queue) that allows a small number of immediate completions inside a window even if the tenant's quota is exhausted. Grace tokens replenish slowly to prevent abuse but are sufficient to finish tail-small work without being demoted. The scheduler integrates KV-cache awareness: requests flagged with KV_PIN score > 0.7 are routed through a soft-pin lane that receives weighted share and has a separate grace reservoir to prevent pin starvation. Finally, we added a lightweight kernel hint API so the serving runtime can prioritize quantized kernels or switch to fused attention paths for long-seq batches to reduce latency variance.

Implementation details: - New scheduler module: src/serving/scheduler/fairshare_time_slice.rs (Rust). Purely opt-in; controlled by runtime config + per-deployment feature flag. - Grace token leaky-bucket implemented as atomic counters per queue + background replenisher tuned by observed request interarrival. - KV soft-pin lane implemented as an additional priority tier inside the window; weights are adjustable via config. - Integration points: runtime dispatch now annotates calls with kernel_hint and kv_pin_score (float). The kernel selection path consults these hints to prefer quantized/fused kernels when beneficial. - New metrics: scheduler.window_count, scheduler.window_utilization, scheduler.grace_tokens_{used,available}, scheduler.kv_lane_utilization. - Unit + integration tests added covering fairness under synthetic workloads, KV-skew scenarios, and grace exhaustion. - Bench harness: perf/bench/scheduler_time_slice/ with scripts to reproduce latency/throughput numbers.

Benchmarks (internal cluster, A100 ext4 region, mixed tenant load): - Baseline (current main): p50=18ms p95=210ms p99=380ms overall throughput=980 rps. - Time-sliced fair-share (this PR): p50=16ms p95=155ms p99=260ms overall throughput=1040 rps. - Under KV-skew (one heavy KV-pinned tenant): baseline p99 spikes to 680ms and low-rate tenants starve; PR reduces p99 to 300ms and preserves small-tenant p99 within +10ms of baseline. Cost per token estimated -7% due to better kernel hints and reduced wasted preemption.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag and cluster-level opt-in. Stage rollout: canary on 1 node pool -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full. Observatory dashboards and alerts (scheduler.window_utilization > 90% for >5m) included in the PR.

Testing & safety: CI includes unit and integration tests; bench harness reproducible scripts included. Toggle disables new code paths, and fallback automatically returns to old scheduler when kernel_hint or kv_pin_score not provided.

Risks & mitigations: - Mis-tuned grace token rates could allow low-priority tenants to overrun windows. Mitigation: conservative defaults and auto-throttle on token burn metrics. - Kernel hint misuse could degrade throughput for some models; mitigation: hints are advisory and we fall back to default kernels on negative perf signals.

Files changed are limited and non-breaking; documented in docs/ops/scheduler.md. See commits for small refactors and test additions.

release_notes: Improves scheduler fairness and p99 latency under KV-skewed loads. Adds time-sliced fair-share windows, grace-token finishers for short requests, and KV soft-pin lane. Opt-in via runtime config. Metrics and dashboards added for rollout.
